reviews.decision_reason: select_demand applies the stated score-threshold path and keeps the explicit fallback identifiers in the selected data path. In the supplied input every corpus record has demand_score >= 3, so this unit should select all eight records before downstream normalization. No behaviorally significant fault is visible in this boundary from the supplied package.

normalize truncates the selected evidence to head(1) via index_window = [0]. That drops valid selected demand records n06-r02 through n06-r08 from the needs handoff even though they are allowed corpus identifiers and were part of the assigned job input. This is behaviorally significant for market-demand review because it hides observed needs, alternatives, and downstream coverage outcomes instead of leaving missing evidence visible. The final recommendation can still be deterministic for n06-r01, but the handoff is materially incomplete.

assemble_provenance ranks the normalized needs deterministically by demand_score descending and record_id, using missing-safe field access. The one-row evidence_sources output matches the one-row normalized input. The upstream incompleteness originates before this boundary, in normalize, not in provenance assembly.
